institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A great location in Europe, with both a vibrant city life and beautiful nature nearby

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find all the necessary information before my departure.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: BOKU University was very helpful when I arrived. They sent several emails with practical information before the semester started and provided a checklist with everything that needed to be done after arrival. This made it easy to keep track of the different steps and made the arrival process well organized.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed at an ÖJAB student residence in the city centre, and I would definitely recommend it. It was easy to arrange, the location was very convenient, and it was a good place to live during my exchange.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: BOKU University is located a bit outside the city centre, so living in the city centre meant I had a slightly longer commute to university. However, I did not have classes every day, only around three days per week, so it still worked well in practice. At the same time, it was nice to live centrally and be close to all the main sights and the city life in Vienna.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: At BOKU University, courses generally have a low number of ECTS points, typically between 1–5 ECTS. Because of this, I spent quite some time selecting enough courses to meet the required workload and making sure that my timetable would work without any overlaps. However, the actual registration process for courses was very easy, as everything was done online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: BOKU University provided an online timetable system that made it easy to check for overlaps between courses. This was very helpful when planning my schedule, as it gave a clear overview of all course times in one place.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was lucky to get a place in the classes I wanted. Many lecturers at BOKU are very aware that exchange students are only there for one semester, and they therefore try to accommodate them as much as possible by helping them get into the courses they need.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a good idea to arrive earlier than the start of the semester. You can only register for courses after you have received your student card, and this can only be issued in person at the university. Course registration is also on a first-come, first-served basis, so it is an advantage to get everything set up as early as possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one bachelor-level course, and this actually turned out to be the most demanding course I had. In comparison, the master-level courses were less demanding in terms of workload and expectations

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Compared to UCPH, the teaching style at BOKU involved much more mandatory attendance, and in some classes you had to sign a sheet to confirm your presence. In several courses, participation also counted as part of the assessment, meaning that how much you contributed in class discussions could influence your grade. Overall, there were not many traditional lectures like the ones I am used to from UCPH, as the teaching was generally more interactive and attendance-based.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

Intercultural competence - Changing perspectives in a diverse (working) environment,
German Intensive Course before the start of the semester,

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would definitely recommend the Food Packaging course, as I learned a lot from it and found it very interesting and relevant within food science.

I would also strongly recommend taking a German course before the semester starts. It was a very social course with mainly Erasmus students, and these were people I continued to meet throughout the rest of the semester, which made it a nice way to build a social network early on.

questions.answer: I did not encounter any unexpected costs during my exchange

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport was more expensive than I expected, as I did not use a bike as I normally do in Denmark. Since I relied more on public transportation in Vienna, this became a larger cost than I had anticipated.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many activities available for Erasmus students, especially social events and trips organized throughout the semester. In addition, USI student sports offered a wide range of different sports and activities

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going hiking outside Vienna, as there are many beautiful 'Stadtwanderweg' that are easy to access and offer great nature experiences close to the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend taking the train from Vienna to explore nearby cities and regions. There are many interesting cities close to Vienna, and it is very easy and convenient to travel by train. For example, Bratislava and Budapest are nearby and easy weekend trips, and within Austria you can also visit cities like Salzburg or Innsbruck. The train system works very well and makes it easy to travel around.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to adjust to the local culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not experience major cultural challenges during my exchange.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated how friendly and welcoming people were. Overall, I did not experience a big cultural difference between Denmark and Austria, which made it very easy to feel comfortable and settle in quickly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Vienna is a great city to go on exchange to. It has a very good size, not too big and not too small, and offers a nice balance between city life and nature nearby. It is also very easy to travel to other countries and cities in the region, as the train connections work very well. In addition, it is relatively close to Denmark, which makes it easy to receive visits from friends and family during the exchange.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a semester where you naturally think a bit less about studying and more about experiencing the city and the country. There is a lot to see and do in and around Vienna, so there are plenty of opportunities to travel and explore during the exchange.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was building a connection to a city outside Denmark. I also really enjoyed meeting people from all over the world and experiencing so many things that I would not normally experience at home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during my exchange was not having enough time to see and experience everything I wanted to. There was so much to do and explore, both in Vienna and in the surrounding areas, which sometimes made it difficult to fit everything into one semester.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
